SMTO-ART-0007 — A file changed while SMTO was saving it

GUID: 4e1da728-bb58-481b-a373-afa4a7a18222
Slug: artifact-changed
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • SMTO was saving a copy of a file from your Task, but the file changed, moved or disappeared during the copy. SMTO didn't keep the half-finished copy.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the Task, wait until every command that writes this file has finished, and don't edit the file yourself in the meantime. SMTO only keeps a copy that matches the file exactly, which needs the file to stop changing.
  2. Open Artifacts from this run and select Retry collection if it appears. If Download all failed, select Download all again. A new attempt reads the file as it is now instead of the version that was changing.
  3. If the file never stops changing, such as a log that is always being written, ask SMTO in a new message to save a finished copy under a new name. A file that keeps changing can't be copied consistently, but a finished copy can.

What success looks like

  • The file appears in Artifacts from this run without an error, or Download all gives you a ZIP file.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, with the file's name. Don't reuse an old link to the file; open it from the current Artifacts list.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Artifact discovery, registration, temp staging or ZIP export detected that the source changed between observation and copy (revision, size, digest or file-identity mismatch, or the file vanished or could not be opened).

What this means

  • Source collection/export observes revision, size, digest or filesystem identity changes, including a race while opening/walking the source. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Source collection/export observes revision, size, digest or filesystem identity changes, including a race while opening/walking the source.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect original expected revision and active writers before collecting again.

How to fix it

  • Find the diagnostic in the run's collection status or the Server/Gateway log (revision mismatch, open/identity failure, export digest mismatch, temp staging or discovery change). Make sure the writing process has exited, then retry collection through the run's artifacts reconcile endpoint or rebuild the export; the collector re-snapshots current revisions instead of reusing stale ones.
  • Wait for writers to finish, rediscover the current source, and collect from a stable snapshot. Verify its size and hash.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A stable authoritative snapshot yields matching identity, complete size and hash.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
